findings.issue: pkill -f patterns matched the agent's own bash command line and killed its own shell, twice, from the same mistake
findings.suggestion: Use bracketed patterns (e.g. pkill -f 'api/server[.]mjs') or PID-based kills after the first occurrence; don't repeat a command that just killed you

findings.issue: Several write calls produced broken code (garbage helpers, missing const, invalid template expressions, '<Not found />') that needed immediate follow-up edits
findings.suggestion: Compose writes more carefully or use the edit tool for targeted fixes; broken-on-arrival writes cost turns and risk shipping if self-review slips

findings.issue: Re-ran the failing test suite twice (filtered) without any new information while the root cause (host binding) was still unknown
findings.suggestion: Diagnose the first failure (reproduce manually, compare curl vs node fetch) before re-running the suite

findings.issue: Initial misreadings of already-viewed reference screenshots caused rework: white summary card removed late, sticky header removed late
findings.suggestion: Sample background pixels / anchor-scroll behavior of the reference screenshots before committing to layout assumptions

findings.issue: Nearly all source edits were inline python string-replacements in bash rather than the edit tool (1 edit call vs 17 bash file writes)
findings.suggestion: Prefer the edit tool for multi-line changes; it's less brittle and gives diff feedback

findings.issue: Miscalled tools: read of a guessed nonexistent path, a heredoc corrupted by repeated junk lines, and a fumbled cd to /home/pi
findings.suggestion: Verify paths with ls before reading; keep shell heredocs short and simple

summary: A disciplined, methodical session: exhaustive up-front exploration, one big scaffold, systematic root-cause debugging (the IPv6 binding fix stands out), and unusually thorough visual verification with pixel-level comparison to every reference screenshot plus a final full test pass after the last edit. The main costs were broken-on-arrival writes, a twice-repeated pkill self-kill, and some screenshot-misreading rework in the long visual-fidelity phase.
